messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point numbers have limited precision, so each operation rounds the exact real‑valued sum to the nearest representable value. Because rounding can introduce a small error, the error incurred when adding a + b first may differ from the error when adding b + c first, and those differences propagate to the final result. Consequently, (a + b) + c and a + (b + c) can produce distinct rounded values, breaking associativity.
